description: Every img must have an alt attribute — empty alt= for decorative images
rationale: Screen readers rely on alt text; missing alt breaks non-visual access

description: Every input must have an associated <label> via for/id or wrapping
rationale: Unlabeled inputs are unusable with assistive tech

description: All interactive elements must be reachable and operable by keyboard
rationale: Many users navigate entirely without a mouse

description: Preserve or style a visible focus indicator — never outline: none alone
rationale: Focus rings are the keyboard user's cursor

description: Maintain WCAG AA contrast: 4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large
rationale: Low contrast excludes users with low vision

description: Use semantic elements (nav, main, button, header) over generic divs
rationale: Semantic HTML gives assistive tech structure for free

description: Prefer native HTML semantics before adding ARIA
rationale: No ARIA is better than wrong ARIA

description: Use one h1 per page and don't skip heading levels
rationale: Screen readers use headings as a navigation table of contents

description: Provide a skip-to-main-content link as the first focusable element
rationale: Skip links bypass repetitive nav for keyboard users

description: Set a valid lang attribute on the html element
rationale: Screen readers use lang to select pronunciation and voice

description: Use <button> for actions and <a> for navigation
rationale: Role confusion breaks keyboard and AT expectations

description: Associate error messages with inputs via aria-describedby
rationale: Unlinked errors aren't announced to screen readers

description: Respect prefers-reduced-motion and disable non-essential animation
Announce dynamic changes with aria-live where appropriate
rationale: Silent updates are invisible to screen reader users
